# Other agents

OUTDATED (2026-11-10): the tool `agents` described on this page was removed. Use the three tools that replaced it and follow each tool's own description: `agents_children` (start agents that are yours, talk to them, stop and remove them), `agents_ctl` (manage any agent on the daemon table), `agent_def` (make or check an agent definition). The calls below are the old ones and will be replaced.

Tool `agents`: start a child agent, talk to it, remove it, list every agent on your daemon.

A child agent runs on the same daemon as you. It does not inherit your brain or your tools; give them explicitly if it needs them.

Two ways to start one:

- from an existing definition: `{"op": "add", "name": "kid", "def": "agents/kid"}`. Options change only this child (they go to its own stack, the definition stays as it is): `"llm": {"model": "fake"}` (which brain pack it uses), `"tools": [{"name": "wall_clock", "path": "tools/wall_clock"}]`, `"tools_rm": ["self_tools"]`.
- by writing a new definition: `{"op": "new", "name": "kid", "path": "defs/kid", "from": "agents/kid", "files": {"system.txt": "You are ..."}}`. `from` is copied to `path` (inside your workspace, must not exist yet), then `files` (full text per file), `llm`, `tools`, `tools_rm` are written into the copy. Without `from`, `files` must hold the whole definition. The folder stays; start it again later with `add` and `"def": "defs/kid"`.

Both take `"ws": "kid_ws"` (the child's workspace: relative to yours, or absolute; default: your own workspace, shared files) and `"limits": {"mem_mb": 512}`.

`new`, `add` and `rm` accept `ctl_timeout_s`: seconds to wait for the daemon to attach or remove the child (default 30, at most 1700); for example, use 120 when the daemon is busy.

Other calls:

- send a message and return at once: `{"op": "say", "name": "kid", "text": "..."}`
- send and wait for the answer: `{"op": "ask", "name": "kid", "text": "...", "timeout_s": 120}` (default 600)
- remove it (its stack is deleted): `{"op": "rm", "name": "kid"}`
- list: `{"op": "ls"}` (one line of JSON: `agents` = the daemon table, `children` = yours, `max_children`)

Rules:

- `def` and `from` are relative to your workspace, or absolute. The folder must declare `aos-agent` in its `interfaces.json`; otherwise `InterfaceMissing`.
- `say`, `ask`, `rm` work only on agents you started yourself. Others give `ChildUnknown`; a child removed by someone else gives `ChildMissing` once and is then forgotten. You may `ls` everyone.
- Two limits. Your own: at most `max_children` children at once (default 4); over it `add` / `new` fail with `ChildSlotMissing` and nothing is started. The daemon's: the judge counts every agent on the daemon; `AddRejected ... SlotMissing` means the daemon is full. Either way remove a child you no longer need, or report that the limit is reached. Do not retry in a loop.
- `AnswerMissing` after `ask`: the child did not answer within `timeout_s`. Check its row with `ls`: if its phase is `stopped` with a `reason`, it crashed (see `status.json`); if it is `running`, it is just slow, ask again with a longer timeout or `say` and come back later.
- Remove children when you are done with them. Nobody removes them for you.

For a one-off task where you want only the conclusion back (the helper is removed afterwards), use tool `thought` instead: see `agents.json#/thought`.

thought:
# Small thought: one task, just the conclusion

The `thought` tool starts a disposable child agent, gives it one task and returns only a short conclusion; the child's tool exchanges do not enter your history. The child definition comes from the call parameter `from`; only when omitted does it use the default in the tool registration's `env.AOS_THOUGHT_FROM`.

Choosing a tool:

- `thought`: one step in a plan, returning one sentence after checking. By default it is removed after answering; no naming, follow-up or manual removal is needed.
- `agents`: an assistant for an ongoing conversation. Name it, ask it questions, and `rm` it yourself.

Calls:

- With a configured default: `{"goal": "Find what time it is and say whether it is morning"}`.
- Choose another definition: `{"from": "helpers/reviewer", "goal": "Review the result and return one sentence"}`.
- Borrow your own tools: `{"goal": "Read the knowledge base and summarize endpoint packs", "tools": [{"name": "memory"}], "max_chars": 200}`.
- A → B → C: call once per step, passing the previous conclusion in `context`, for example `"context": ["Step A concluded: the config is in cfg/"]`.

Rules:

- Put the default in this agent's thought tool registration, for example `{"path": "../../lib/agent/thought", "env": {"AOS_THOUGHT_FROM": "helpers/basic"}}`. You can also use `--envs AOS_THOUGHT_FROM=helpers/basic` when registering the tool. The env value is passed literally, not resolved relative to the registry file; both `from` and this default resolve relative to your workspace `$AOS_WS`, while absolute paths are used as given. Store relative paths for portability. The definition must declare the `aos-agent` public interface. If neither is supplied, the result is `FromMissing`; no template is guessed. An explicitly blank value or wrong type gives `ArgumentsBad`, without falling back to the default.
- The child receives `goal` and `context` on top of its definition's existing settings. State clearly in `goal` what it should return.
- Tools: omitted `tools` keeps the definition's tool set; `[]` clears it; a list keeps only those tools. `{"name": "memory"}` without `path` borrows your own tool of that name; with `path`, that path is used. Overlays follow the definition's `interfaces.json` declarations.
- Brain: defaults to yours; `model` can select another pack. If your brain settings cannot be read (for example, a sandbox cannot see the definition), an error is returned, commonly `InterfaceMissing`; you can supply `model` explicitly.
- Depth is read from the startup environment's `AOS_THOUGHT_DEPTH` (unset means 0); the child starts with the parent's depth plus 1. Calling again at depth 2 gives `DepthExceeded`.
- `keep: true` stops and keeps the child after answering, appending `details: procs/<name>/` (relative to the daemon) to the conclusion. For a follow-up, first run `aos-agent ctl start --target <name>`, then `say`/`listen`.
- `AnswerMissing`: no answer within `timeout_s` (default 600; any finite positive number); the error line ends with `(details: ...)`, and the stack is kept for human inspection. `DepthExceeded`: the depth limit was reached; do this step yourself. `ToolMissing`: you do not have the same-named tool to borrow. `ArgumentsBad`: `goal` is missing or blank, or a parameter is invalid. `DaemonMissing`: `AOS_DAEMON` is unset or its directory does not exist. `DaemonFailed`: the daemon is configured and its directory exists, but no reply arrived within the timeout (it may be busy, paused or down). Do this step yourself or explain that it is temporarily unavailable; try at most once more later, without a retry loop.
